sentences.text: In the third summer they came back on the eleventh of May, and on the fourteenth one of them landed.
Ada was on the fire escape.

It came in off the loop, fast and flat the way they do, and instead of pulling up it went straight at the wall of the flats — at the point where the render had come away above her bedroom window, leaving a gap about the width of two fingers — and folded, and went in.
She did not move for a long time.
There had been a swift nest above her bedroom window and she had not known, and the reason she had not known was that a swift going into a hole does not slow down first.
There is no landing.
There is a bird at forty miles an hour and then there is no bird.
She told Mr Iqbal the next morning and he came up the stairs, which he did not do, and stood in the yard with his head back for a quarter of an hour.
"Above the window," he said.
"Yes." "Above your window." "Yes." He put his hands in his pockets.
"You understand what that means," he said.
"That bird has been coming back to that hole every May since before that render came off, probably.
They use the same hole.
They use it for years.

Which means for the whole time you were lying in that bed noticing that they never land — that one was landing about a metre and a half above your head, six times a day, for three months a year." Ada thought about that for the rest of the summer and has thought about it, on and off, for twenty years since.
She is at university now, doing something entirely unrelated, and she goes home in May.
The render has still not been fixed.
She has asked, twice, in writing, that it not be fixed, and has had one letter back from the housing office that did not really engage with the question.
She sits on the fire escape at eleven at night when she is home, and the loops go over, and she cannot tell one from another and never could.

Somewhere in that noise is a bird that has not touched the ground since April, and will not until next April, and is going to sleep tonight two kilometres above the retail park with half its head switched off.
She finds that she thinks about it whenever she is having a difficult week.
Not as a comfort exactly.
More as a fact she likes having available: that while she is doing whatever she is doing, badly, in a small room, something is up there going round.
